chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from al-Rabi' ibn Muhammad al-Musli, from Abi al-Rabi' al-Shami, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
No worship of God is better than being quiet and walking to his house.

key_terms.بَيْتِهِ: His house (referring to the person's home)

ai.seo_question: What is considered the best form of worship according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), emphasizing that *al-samt* (silence/quietude) and *al-mashy ila al-bayt* (walking to one's home) constitute the pinnacle of worship by fostering inner reflection and minimizing social distractions. This teaching aligns with the Shia emphasis on *khushu'* (humility and focus) in private devotion, distinguishing it from performative public piety. The act of returning home is thus elevated to a spiritual journey, reinforcing the sanctity of the domestic sphere as a place of worship.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 2-8 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted on the authority of Ayoob ibn Nooh, on the authority of Al-Rabi’a ibn Muhammad al-Muslimy, on the authority of Abil Rabi’a ash-Shamy, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), “
No worship of God is better than being quiet and walking to God’s House.”
